title: THE SIN WE DID NOT INTEND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Say to the Israelites: "When anyone sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD's commands—"'" - Lev 4:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Unintentionally. That single word shapes this entire chapter.

This is not about defiance. Leviticus deals elsewhere with the person who sins with a high hand, in open rebellion. Chapter 4 is about the sin you did not plan — the word that slipped out, the corner you cut without thinking, the person you failed without noticing, the commandment you broke because you had forgotten it was there.

And here is the uncomfortable truth the verse teaches: unintentional sin is still sin. It still required a sacrifice. Ignorance reduced the guilt; it did not erase it.

Most of us handle this badly. We reserve the word "sin" for deliberate wrongdoing and quietly excuse everything else as personality, pressure, or oversight. God does not grade on intention alone. He grades on truth.

David understood this. He prayed, "Who can discern their own errors? Forgive my hidden faults" (Ps 19:12). Paul said, "My conscience is clear, but that does not make me innocent. It is the Lord who judges me" (1 Cor 4:4).

This should humble us — and then it should send us running to Christ with enormous relief. His blood covers not only the sins I can name, but the ones I never noticed. Nothing in your life is hidden from Him, and nothing is beyond His cleansing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I only take seriously the sins I chose deliberately?
2. Am I willing to ask God to show me faults I cannot see in myself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive not only what I know I have done but what I have never noticed. Search me, and cleanse me completely. Amen.
